newsitem.title: UK: UK urged to crack down on arms embargo violators.
newsitem.headline: UK urged to crack down on arms embargo violators.

text.p: Human Rights Watch on Monday urged Britain to do a better job overseeing companies operating on its soil and ensuring they do not violate international arms embargoes.

Britain recently began investigating allegations that Mil-Tech Corp. Ltd, incorporated on the Isle of Man, was involved in supplying more than $5.5 million worth of weapons and ammunition used in the 1994 genocide in Rwanda. "In light of these allegations, Human Rights Watch calls on the British government to seize the opportunity to draft clearer laws to investigate and prosecute those who facilitate the delivery of weapons despite international arms embargoes," the group said in a statement released in Washington.

While Britain incorporated the U.N. arms embargo against Rwanda in June 1994, the Isle of Man, an offshore island possession of Britain's, did not follow the usual practice of copying Britain in such matters.

The British government has said there was no indication from the allegations about Mil-Tech that the arms were exported from Britain and no license had been issued to Mil-Tec. "Too often individuals circumvent United Nations arms embargoes by organising the supply of weapons through third countries," said Joost Hilterman, director of the Human Rights Watch Arms Project.

They cannot simply cast off their obligations by saying that no weapons were exported directly from their countries," he said. The group said Britain and the Isle of Man should immediately incorporate U.N. embargoes into their national laws. The same should apply to European Union arms embargoes in Britain's case. Britain should require individuals and companies to register with the government if they are involved in the supply, delivery or arrangement of weapons shipments via third countries. Additionally Britain should improve inter-departmental coordination in overseeing companies or individuals known to be involved in or suspected of arms trading, it said.
